title: Florida Faces Its Largest Dengue Outbreak in Decades
subtitle: Health officials are working to control the spread of the mosquito-borne virus in the Tampa area.

summary.en: Florida is currently experiencing its largest outbreak of dengue fever in many decades. Health officials have reported over 250 locally acquired cases, mostly in Hillsborough County. The virus is spread by mosquitoes, which are expanding their range due to warmer weather. While many people experience mild symptoms, the disease can cause severe pain and, in rare cases, death. Authorities are now taking emergency measures to reduce the mosquito population and protect the public.
summary.zh: 佛羅里達州目前正經歷數十年來最大規模的登革熱疫情。衛生官員已通報超過 250 例本土感染病例，主要集中在希爾斯波羅郡。該病毒由蚊子傳播，由於氣候變暖，蚊子的活動範圍正在擴大。雖然許多人僅出現輕微症狀，但該疾病可能導致劇烈疼痛，在罕見情況下甚至會致命。當局目前正採取緊急措施以減少蚊子數量並保護民眾。

paragraphs.en: Florida is currently dealing with a significant health challenge as it faces the largest outbreak of dengue fever in the continental United States in decades. According to MedPage Today, state health officials have reported more than 250 cases of the virus that were caught locally. This means the people who became sick did not travel to another country to get the disease; instead, they were bitten by infected mosquitoes right in their own neighborhoods. The vast majority of these cases have been found in Hillsborough County, which includes the city of Tampa.
paragraphs.zh: 佛羅里達州目前正應對一項重大的健康挑戰，該州正面臨數十年來美國本土最大規模的登革熱疫情。根據醫學新聞網站 MedPage Today 的報導，州衛生官員已通報超過 250 例本土感染病例。這意味著染病者並未前往其他國家，而是在自家社區被帶有病毒的蚊子叮咬。這些病例絕大多數集中在包含坦帕市在內的希爾斯波羅郡。

paragraphs.en: To understand why this is happening, it is helpful to look at the nature of the virus. Dengue is spread to humans through the bites of a specific type of mosquito. Many people who catch the virus do not feel sick at all. However, others may experience fever, flu-like symptoms, and intense body aches. Because of this extreme pain, the disease is sometimes called "breakbone fever." In very serious cases, the virus can cause internal bleeding, shock, and even death. MedPage Today reported that one elderly woman in Tampa died from the virus on September 4.
paragraphs.zh: 要了解為何會發生這種情況，觀察病毒的特性很有幫助。登革熱是透過特定種類蚊子的叮咬傳播給人類。許多感染者完全不會感到不適，但其他人可能會出現發燒、類流感症狀以及劇烈的身體疼痛。由於這種極度的疼痛，該疾病有時被稱為「斷骨熱」。在極為嚴重的情況下，病毒可能導致內出血、休克甚至死亡。MedPage Today 報導稱，坦帕市一名老婦人已於 9 月 4 日因感染該病毒而過世。

paragraphs.en: For a long time, most dengue cases in the United States were found in people who had recently traveled to other parts of the world where the disease is common, such as Puerto Rico. While Puerto Rico continues to see high numbers of cases, the situation in Florida is different because the virus is now spreading locally. MedPage Today noted that the state’s previous worst year for locally acquired cases was 2023, when just under 200 cases were reported. The current outbreak in the Tampa area, which began in July, is already on track to be the largest since at least the 1940s.
paragraphs.zh: 長期以來，美國大多數的登革熱病例都是在近期曾前往波多黎各等疾病流行地區的民眾身上發現。雖然波多黎各的病例數依然偏高，但佛羅里達州的情況不同，因為病毒目前正在當地傳播。MedPage Today 指出，該州先前本土病例最嚴重的年份是 2023 年，當時通報了近 200 例。而自 7 月開始的坦帕地區疫情，目前已成為自 1940 年代以來規模最大的一次。

paragraphs.en: Experts point to several reasons for this rise. Dawn Wesson, a disease expert from Tulane University, explained that Florida often sees dengue because the state receives many travelers from places where the virus is common. Once the virus arrives, it needs the right environment to spread. The mosquitoes that carry dengue prefer warm weather. As the climate changes, these mosquitoes are able to live in more places and stay active for longer periods. This allows the virus to move into new areas where people do not have natural protection or immunity against it.
paragraphs.zh: 專家指出造成此現象的原因有幾點。杜蘭大學 (Tulane University) 的疾病專家韋森 (Dawn Wesson) 解釋說，佛羅里達州經常出現登革熱，是因為該州接收了許多來自病毒流行地區的旅客。一旦病毒進入，就需要合適的環境來傳播。傳播登革熱的蚊子偏好溫暖的天氣。隨著氣候變遷，這些蚊子能在更多地方生存並維持更長時間的活躍期。這使得病毒能夠進入人們對其缺乏天然保護力或免疫力的新區域。

paragraphs.en: Developing a vaccine—a medicine that helps the body fight off a disease—has been difficult because there are four different types of the dengue virus. According to MedPage Today, if a person is infected with one type, their body builds protection against that specific type for life. However, if they later catch a different type of the virus, their immune system might not work correctly. In some cases, the body's reaction can actually help the virus grow, making it harder to create a single vaccine that works for everyone.
paragraphs.zh: 開發疫苗（一種協助身體對抗疾病的藥物）之所以困難，是因為登革熱病毒有四種不同的類型。根據 MedPage Today 的說法，如果一個人感染了其中一種，身體會對該特定類型產生終身免疫。然而，如果他們之後感染了另一種不同類型的病毒，免疫系統可能無法正確運作。在某些情況下，身體的反應反而可能助長病毒增殖，這使得研發出一種對所有人都有效的單一疫苗變得更加困難。

paragraphs.en: In response to the growing number of cases, officials in Hillsborough and nearby counties have declared local emergencies. This allows them to use more resources to fight the outbreak. Workers in the Tampa area are currently spraying chemicals day and night to reduce the number of mosquitoes. The goal is to lower the population of these insects quickly to stop the virus from spreading further to other people.
paragraphs.zh: 為了應對不斷增加的病例，希爾斯波羅郡及鄰近地區的官員已宣布進入地方緊急狀態。這使他們能動用更多資源來對抗疫情。坦帕地區的工作人員目前正日以繼夜地噴灑化學藥劑，以減少蚊子數量。目標是迅速降低這些昆蟲的族群數量，以阻止病毒進一步傳播給其他人。

paragraphs.en: While the numbers in Florida are high for the continental United States, they are still small compared to global figures. The World Health Organization has reported more than 2.2 million infections and nearly 1,200 deaths worldwide this year. Within the United States, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reports that there have been nearly 1,900 locally acquired cases this year, with the majority occurring in Puerto Rico.
paragraphs.zh: 雖然佛羅里達州的數據在美國本土來看偏高，但與全球數據相比仍屬少數。世界衛生組織 (WHO) 報告顯示，今年全球已有超過 220 萬例感染，近 1,200 人死亡。在美國境內，疾病管制與預防中心 (CDC) 指出，今年已有近 1,900 例本土感染病例，其中大多數發生在波多黎各。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, it is unclear exactly how the situation will develop. While the current emergency measures are focused on the Tampa area, experts continue to monitor the spread of these mosquitoes across other parts of the country. For now, the main priority for Florida health officials remains controlling the mosquito population and educating the public on how to avoid bites. As the weather stays warm, the risk of transmission remains a serious concern for the state.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，情況將如何發展尚不明朗。雖然目前的緊急措施集中在坦帕地區，但專家持續監控這些蚊子在全國其他地區的擴散情形。目前，佛羅里達州衛生官員的首要任務仍是控制蚊子數量，並教育大眾如何避免叮咬。隨著天氣持續溫暖，傳播風險對該州而言仍是一項嚴重的隱憂。

sources.title: Florida's Dengue Outbreak Is Now the Largest in the Continental U.S. in Decades

quiz.question: According to the article, what distinguishes the current Florida dengue outbreak from previous years?

options.A: It is the first time the virus has been detected in the Tampa area.
options.B: The number of locally acquired cases has already surpassed the total from 2023.
options.C: It is the first time an elderly person has died from the virus in the United States.
options.D: The virus has mutated into a new, more dangerous form that is harder to treat.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第三段明確指出，2023 年是先前紀錄中本地感染案例最多的一年（不到 200 例），而目前的爆發規模已經超越此紀錄，成為自 1940 年代以來最嚴重的一次。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章未提及這是首次在 Tampa 發現；選項 C 錯誤，文中僅提到一位老婦人死亡，並未說是美國史上首例；選項 D 錯誤，文中提到疫苗開發困難是因為有四種病毒類型，而非病毒突變成新形態。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about why dengue is becoming a greater concern in the continental United States?

options.A: Travelers from Puerto Rico are intentionally bringing the virus to Florida.
options.B: The local population has developed a natural immunity that is now failing.
options.C: Changing environmental conditions are creating a more suitable habitat for disease-carrying mosquitoes.
options.D: Medical professionals have only recently learned how to diagnose the virus correctly.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第四段，專家指出氣候變遷使得蚊子能在更多地方生存並延長活躍期，這讓病毒得以擴散至原本沒有免疫力的地區。選項 A 錯誤，文中提到旅行者帶來病毒，但未暗示是蓄意行為；選項 B 與文意相反，文中提到人們缺乏自然免疫力；選項 D 在文中未提及，且並非造成爆發的主要原因。

quiz.question: In the sentence 'The current outbreak in the Tampa area, which began in July, is already on track to be the largest since at least the 1940s,' what does the phrase 'on track' mean?

options.A: Moving toward a specific result or outcome.
options.B: Following a physical path or railroad line.
options.C: Experiencing a sudden decrease in speed.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在文中 'on track' 的意思是「朝著某個目標或結果發展」。選項 B 是該片語的字面意思，但在這裡不適用；選項 C 與 D 的含義與文意完全相反，因為 'on track' 在此語境下代表趨勢正朝向成為史上最大規模的爆發發展，而非減緩或延遲。

quiz.question: What is the primary focus of this article?

options.A: To explain the biological process of how dengue virus affects the human immune system.
options.B: To compare the death rates of dengue fever in Florida versus the rest of the world.
options.C: To provide a historical timeline of all dengue outbreaks in the United States since the 1940s.
options.D: To report on the current local dengue outbreak in Florida and the factors contributing to its spread.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。這篇文章的核心在於報導佛羅里達州目前面臨的登革熱疫情，並探討造成此次疫情的原因（如氣候變遷、蚊子傳播）以及應對措施。選項 A 僅是文章的一小部分內容；選項 B 只是文中用來對比的數據，並非主旨；選項 C 錯誤，文章並未提供完整的歷史時間軸，僅提到 1940 年代作為比較的基準點。
